html:
The Liberation Front of the Slovene People was a resistance movement founded in Ljubljana on 26 April 1941, after Germany, Italy and Hungary divided Slovenia among themselves.

The Communist Party led it together with Christian Socialists and liberal groups, and its partisans fought the occupiers in the woods and hills, as part of Tito's Yugoslav army. Italy fenced Ljubljana with barbed wire. The war also became a civil war: Catholic conservatives formed a Home Guard that worked with the occupiers. In 1945 the partisans won, and thousands of Home Guards returned from Austria by the British were killed without trial. The communists then ruled Slovenia inside Yugoslavia until 1990.
sum: The Liberation Front of the Slovene People was a resistance movement founded in Ljubljana on 26 April 1941, after Germany, Italy and Hungary divided Slovenia among themselves.
